fix(engine): preserve native worktree ownership during branch recovery

LynCo-Patches: F02, F09, F10
Source: 795f80012036d4ed53533cf2378d2c20195a2b8f

Retain literal Git argv, distinguish failed inspection from proven absence, preserve assigned nonterminal checkouts across naming changes, and honor a cleanup refusal before clearing assignment. Windows regenerable-artifact removal does not follow junction targets.

Simplify the donor's patch-id fallback: one bounded upstream history stream and one patch-id child replace a per-ancestor two-process loop. An unavailable history remains unknown, never deletion evidence. New real-Git tests force the fallback and its failure path. Correct the junction fixture's ignore rule for POSIX symlinks without weakening Windows coverage.

Validation: selected upstream reproductions fail 6 and pass 7 cases. Final neighboring suite passes 210 tests; 8 native-Windows-only cases are skipped on Linux/Node 22.16.0. This is not Windows process or packaged-runtime qualification.

Delete-when: upstream preserves literal Git arguments, assigned dirty worktrees and junction targets; failed probes never authorize removal; equivalent-patch recovery is bounded without per-ancestor process fanout.
